strategy.concept: We ran our own weekly card-selection ranker on a repeated internal question and show where it broke.
strategy.audience: Small AI/automation studios of 1-5 people who already run some AI workflow but track it in spreadsheets.
strategy.objective: Show one honest process teardown with a specific, checkable number, not a generic AI tip.
strategy.promise: One repeatable check you can run on your own ranking before you trust it.
strategy.rationale: The reference reel got 9.1x its own author's median play by admitting a process gap instead of selling a fix; we mirror the structure, not the topic.

filter.process: Every Monday our ranker picks the week's candidate reels from the eligible pool and writes the shot-plan columns automatically.
filter.friction: The ranker sorted a 654-view reel above a 25,000-view one because it ranks by save-rate, which is not view-normalised.
filter.ai_boundary: The model proposes the ranked order; a human still reads the transcript and contact sheet before anything is scripted.
filter.next_action: Add a view-floor gate before the save-rate sort ships in next week's run.

hooks.text: Our own ranking script put a 654-view reel above a 25,000-view one. Here is why.
Would you trust a ranker that can't tell 654 views from 25,000?
We found the exact line of code that broke our card ranking.

sections.text: Our own ranking script put a 654-view reel above a 25,000-view one. Here is why.
Every Monday our ranker reads the week's eligible reels and writes a shot plan automatically, no human in the loop yet.
It ranks by save-rate per thousand views, not by raw views, so a small reel with a high ratio can outrank a much bigger one.
That is fine when both reels have enough views to trust the ratio. It breaks when one of them barely has any.
This week it picked a 654-view reel over one with 25,000 views, because the small one had a slightly higher save-rate.
We are adding a minimum-view floor before the save-rate sort even runs, so a tiny sample can't win on ratio alone.
We are testing the fix next week and will say here if it held.
